SEAL – Software Engineering Hackathon Management System
Hệ thống Quản lý Cuộc thi SEAL Hackathon ngành Kỹ thuật Phần mềm

This Software Requirements Specification (SRS) describes the functional and non-functional requirements for SEAL – Software Engineering Hackathon Management System. It is intended for the development team, faculty supervisor, and all stakeholders involved in SWP391 at FPT University HCMC.

The purpose of SEAL is to digitize and automate the management workflow of the SEAL Hackathon competition organized by the Software Engineering Department in collaboration with PDP. The system replaces manual, error-prone processes (spreadsheet-based scoring, form-based registration) with an integrated digital platform that also governs the program at an organizational level (event approval, budgeting, and cross-event analytics).

SEAL (Software Engineering Agile League) is an academic hackathon organized up to three times per year (Spring, Summer, Fall) by FPT University HCMC's SE Department, and may host events across multiple disciplines. Each event includes multiple competition rounds (e.g., Preliminary and Final) and is open to students from multiple universities.
The SEAL system covers the complete lifecycle of hackathon management:
Program governance: event approval, term/discipline event quotas, and budget approval
RBL (Research-Based Learning) module for inter-rater reliability analysis

This SRS is organized as follows: Section 1 (Introduction); Section 2 (Overall Description); Section 3 (Functional Requirements); Section 4 (Non-Functional Requirements); Section 5 (System Architecture); Section 6 (Data Requirements); Section 7 (RBL Research Component); Section 8 (Work Breakdown Structure); Section 9 (Use Case Summary); Section 10 (Appendix); Section 11 (Actor Hierarchy); Section 12 (Actor-Feature Matrix); and Section 13 (Business Rules).

SEAL is a standalone web application. It replaces the current manual hackathon management workflow at FPT University HCMC's SE Department and adds an organizational governance layer above day-to-day event operation. The system optionally interfaces with external services (GitHub/GitLab API for repository metadata, a Python statistics library for RBL analysis).
The system is accessed via web browser. No mobile application is required in this version. The backend exposes RESTful APIs consumed by the React frontend.

FR-TEAM-02: Team size is constrained to minimum 3 and maximum 5 members.
FR-TEAM-03: Team Leaders can invite members by email. Invitees must have an approved account.
FR-TEAM-04: Teams register for exactly one category per event, subject to the registration window.
FR-TEAM-05: Coordinators can view all registered teams per event/category and approve or reject registrations.
FR-TEAM-06: Team Leaders can update team name and member composition before the event begins.
FR-TEAM-07: Members can leave a team before the event starts; the system enforces the minimum team size constraint.
FR-SUB-01: Team Leaders submit deliverables per round via URLs: repository (GitHub/GitLab), live demo, and report/slide link.
FR-SUB-02: Submissions are locked after the round deadline. Late submissions are rejected by the system.
FR-SUB-03: Team Leaders can resubmit (update URLs) before the deadline; the system logs submission history with timestamps.

Judges score each submission against each criterion for the round. Scores are numeric within the defined range.
Each judge's scores per criterion per submission are stored separately. No aggregation at input time.
Judges see an interface listing assigned teams with submission links and score input fields per criterion.
Every scoring action is logged: judge ID, team ID, criterion, score value, timestamp, IP. Logs are immutable.
Judges may update scores before the coordinator locks the round. Each modification creates a new audit entry.
Optional calibration phase: judges score a sample submission; the system shows score distribution across judges.
FR-RNK-01: The system automatically computes team rankings per round within each category from aggregated judge scores (weighted average across criteria).
FR-RNK-02: Rankings are computed at event level (across all categories) and category level separately.
FR-RNK-03: The system applies promotion rules: the top N teams per category are automatically marked qualified for the next round.
FR-RNK-04: Coordinators can manually disqualify a team or submission (rule violation). The reason must be recorded; disqualified results are excluded from rankings.
FR-RNK-05: All disqualification actions are logged in the audit trail.
FR-RNK-06: Rankings are visible to coordinators immediately; results are published to participants only when the coordinator triggers publication.
FR-AWD-01: Coordinators assign awards (1st, 2nd, 3rd, special) to teams based on final rankings.
FR-AWD-02: The system sends result notifications (email or in-app) to participants upon publication.
FR-AWD-03: Participants can view published rankings and awards for each round and the overall event.
FR-AWD-04: Coordinators can export full ranking results and scores as CSV/Excel for reporting.

This module captures the organizational cost of an event – including the additional cost of inviting guest judges. Budget approval is part of event approval (performed by the Super Coordinator). It is for planning/approval only; no payment processing is involved.
When proposing an event, the Coordinator attaches an itemized budget. Each line item has a category, description, quantity, unit cost, and computed amount.
Supported categories include at minimum: VENUE, PRIZE, GUEST_JUDGE_FEE, MATERIALS, CATERING, MARKETING, OTHER.
The budget records the planned number of guest judges and the fee per guest judge; the system computes total guest-judge cost as a GUEST_JUDGE_FEE line.

NFR-PERF-01: 95% of API requests respond within 2 seconds under normal load (up to 100 concurrent users).
NFR-PERF-02: Ranking computation for up to 200 teams completes within 5 seconds.
NFR-PERF-03: Supports at least 500 registered users and 100 concurrent active sessions.
NFR-PERF-04: Cross-event analytics over up to 20 events returns within 5 seconds (consider pre-aggregating summary metrics at event completion).
NFR-SEC-01: All API endpoints (except registration and login) require a valid JWT token.
NFR-SEC-02: Passwords stored using bcrypt hashing (minimum cost factor 10).
NFR-SEC-03: Role-based access control: no user can access resources beyond their assigned role.
NFR-SEC-04: All HTTP communication uses HTTPS in production.
NFR-SEC-05: Audit logs are append-only and cannot be modified or deleted by any role, including Admin and Super Coordinator.
NFR-SEC-06: SQL injection and XSS mitigated via parameterized queries and input validation.
NFR-SEC-07: System-configuration and role-provisioning endpoints are accessible only to ADMIN; event-approval endpoints only to SUPER_COORDINATOR. Cross-axis access attempts return 403.
NFR-USE-01: Responsive and functional on desktop browsers (Chrome, Firefox, Edge). Minimum viewport width 1024px.
NFR-USE-02: The scoring interface is usable by judges with no prior training within 10 minutes of onboarding.
NFR-USE-03: Error messages are in English and actionable (what went wrong and how to fix it).
NFR-REL-01: Targets 99% uptime during active competition periods.
NFR-REL-02: Database backups performed at minimum daily.
NFR-REL-03: Handles database connection failures gracefully with user-facing error messages.
NFR-MNT-01: Backend follows a layered architecture (Controller → Service → Repository).
NFR-MNT-02: All API endpoints documented using Swagger/OpenAPI.
NFR-MNT-03: Unit tests cover at least 60% of business logic (Service layer).

This section defines the role hierarchy and inheritance relationships between actors. v1.2 introduces two new roles – Admin (platform) and Super Coordinator (program) – organized along three separated axes: Admin runs the platform, Super Coordinator runs the program, and the Event Coordinator runs an individual event.

Admin sits at L0 because it provisions every other account, but its authority is technical, not competitive – it is not “above” the Super Coordinator on program decisions. The two axes are separate.

Admin governs the platform (accounts, config, security); Super Coordinator governs the program (events, budgets, policy). Neither overrides the other's domain. Admin cannot approve events; Super Coordinator cannot provision system roles or change system configuration.
Event approval and program policy belong exclusively to the SUPER_COORDINATOR role. Event Coordinators hold no program-wide override.
An event must be approved by a Super Coordinator who is not its creator/owner. Self-approval is rejected by the system.
Admin, Super Coordinator, and Event Coordinator are all prohibited from entering scores. Scoring is exclusive to Judge roles.
A faculty member may be Mentor for Category A and Judge for Category B in the same event, but never both for the same category.
Guest Judge accounts are coordinator-created (no self-registration) and scoped exclusively to assigned rounds. They cannot view other rounds, teams, or event configuration.
Each team has exactly one Team Leader. Leadership transfer before the event start is by the current Leader; after start it requires Coordinator approval.
A user's role is scoped per event. The same user can have different roles in different events.
Permissions: C = Create, R = Read, U = Update, D = Delete, X = Execute/Trigger, — = No Access.
Business Rules define the constraints, policies, and domain logic that govern system behavior. They must be enforced by the backend and cannot be overridden by any role unless explicitly stated.
Each email may be registered once only. Duplicate registration is rejected with an appropriate error.

No account (except Guest Judge accounts created by a Coordinator, or staff accounts provisioned by Admin) may access protected features until approved. Pending accounts are read-only at the login screen only.
An FPT Student must provide a valid FPT student code. External students must provide a student code AND university name. Both are stored and visible to Coordinators.
Guest Judge accounts are scoped to specific rounds. After assigned rounds are completed and locked, they are deactivated automatically or by the Coordinator.
Passwords: minimum 8 characters, at least one uppercase letter and one number. Stored using bcrypt (cost factor ≥ 10). Plain-text passwords are never stored or logged.
Event Has At Least One Round
An event cannot be opened unless it has at least one configured Round with a valid submission deadline.
Rounds are numbered sequentially. Round N+1 cannot begin before Round N is completed and locked by the Coordinator.
The sum of all scoring criteria weights within a Round must equal exactly 100%, validated before the round is activated.
A Mentor for Category A cannot also be Judge for the same Category A; they may judge Category B in the same event.
Once a Round is locked, its criteria, deadlines, and judge assignments are immutable. Only Coordinators may unlock a round, which creates an audit entry.
At Least One Judge per Round
A Round cannot be activated for scoring unless at least one Judge (internal or guest) is assigned to it.
A team must have 3–5 members (incl. the Team Leader) at registration. Falling below 3 after the event starts flags the team for Coordinator review.
One Team per User per Event
A user may belong to at most one team per event.
One Category per Team per Event
A team registers for exactly one Category per event. Category change after registration requires Coordinator approval.
Team registration is only permitted within the event's registration window. Registrations outside the window are rejected.
Each team has exactly one Team Leader. If the Leader leaves, leadership must be transferred before the departure is confirmed.
A user already in a team for the same event cannot be invited to another team in that event; the invitation is rejected with a clear error.
Submissions after the deadline are rejected. Deadline extensions require the Coordinator to update the deadline before the original expiry.
A submission is accepted only if the repository URL is provided. Demo and slide URLs are recommended; the system warns (not blocks) if absent.
One Active Submission per Team per Round
One active submission per round; resubmission before the deadline replaces the previous one. Full version history with timestamps is retained.
Disqualified teams cannot submit. A team disqualified after submitting has its submission marked invalid and excluded from scoring/ranking.
Promoted Teams Only in Next Round
Only teams marked 'promoted' after a round may submit in the subsequent round; others are rejected.
Each score must be within [0, max_score] of the criterion. Out-of-range values are rejected at input validation.
Scores from different judges for the same submission are stored separately. Aggregation only happens during ranking computation.
A Judge can only score rounds explicitly assigned by the Coordinator. Other attempts return 403 Forbidden.
Admin, Super Coordinator, and Coordinator roles are prohibited from entering scores, regardless of context. This cannot be overridden and preserves audit integrity.
Once a round is locked, no Judge may add or modify scores. Unlocking requires Coordinator action and creates an immutable audit entry.
A judge's evaluation is complete only when all criteria are scored. Incomplete scorecards are flagged to the Coordinator.
Any update to a saved score (before lock) creates a new audit entry recording old value, new value, judge ID, timestamp. The original entry is preserved.
Rankings are computed at two levels: category-level (within a category) and event-level (all non-disqualified teams across categories).
Final score = SUM(average_score_per_criterion × weight_of_criterion) across all criteria. The per-criterion average is across all judges who scored that submission.
Ties broken by: (1) higher score on the highest-weighted criterion; (2) next-highest criterion; (3) earlier submission timestamp. Remaining ties go to Coordinator manual resolution.
Disqualified teams are excluded from all ranking computations; their scores are retained for audit but not aggregated.
Top N teams per category (N configured per round) are marked promoted. If fewer than N teams exist, all are promoted.
Rankings and scores are hidden from Team Leaders/Members until the Coordinator publishes results. Coordinator internal visibility is always on.
A Coordinator must provide a written, non-blank reason when disqualifying a team. The reason is recorded in the audit log.
Disqualification removes a team from all current and future rankings in the event; historical scores are preserved but flagged excluded.
A Coordinator may reinstate a team if disqualified in error. Reinstatement requires a reason, creates an audit entry, and recovers previous scores.
The system notifies the Team Leader (in-app, optionally email) with the stated reason.
Audit entries are append-only. No user, including Admin, Super Coordinator, and Coordinator, can modify or delete an entry. The application DB user must not have DELETE privilege on audit_log.

Always logged: (1) Score created; (2) Score updated; (3) Round locked/unlocked; (4) Team disqualified/reinstated; (5) Account approved/rejected; (6) Results published; (7) Event submitted; (8) Event approved; (9) Event rejected (with reason); (10) Budget approved / re-approval triggered; (11) Discipline or quota changed; (12) Staff account created/deactivated; (13) Role assigned/revoked; (14) System configuration changed.
The full audit log is viewable by Admin and Super Coordinator; Coordinators see only their own events; other roles see only their own history.
Only the SUPER_COORDINATOR role may approve events, set quotas, and manage disciplines. Coordinators hold no program-wide override.
An event must be approved by a Super Coordinator who is not its creator/owner. Self-approval is rejected by the system.
An event cannot transition to Open unless it is Approved. Opening an unapproved event is rejected.
Rejecting a proposal requires a non-blank reason, logged and shown to the owning Coordinator.
Non-archived events per term per discipline cannot exceed the configured quota.
Modifying an Approved budget reverts the event to Pending Approval and requires fresh approval.
Admin, Super Coordinator, and Coordinator are prohibited from entering scores, in any context. Cannot be overridden.
The Admin cannot approve events, set quotas/disciplines, manage budgets, or score. The Super Coordinator cannot provision system roles or change system configuration.
Only the Admin may create staff accounts and assign/revoke the SUPER_COORDINATOR and COORDINATOR roles.
All Admin actions (account create/deactivate, role change, config change) generate immutable audit entries; the Admin cannot delete audit entries.
End of Document – SEAL SRS v1.2
